text: Exam #1 Review Guide Format: 110 points • 21 Multiple Choice (3 pts each) • Workout Problem (27 points) – I will provide a list of transactions and adjusting entries. You will record the entries using the financial statement effects worksheet and answer questions about transactions/financial statements. • Workout Problem (20 points) – Calculate ratios excluding price earnings ratio, dividend yield and dividend payout. You might be asked if liquidity or solvency ratios are good/bad/inconclusive. Provided on test: Financial Ratios Chapters 1 & 4 Topics Types of business entities – pros and cons of each type Users of financial statements Accounting definition Accounting standards and accounting rule setters 4 financial statements Types of accounts/categories within each financial statement Order of balance sheet Asset vs expense (future benefit vs immediate benefit) Asset – historical cost vs market value Current vs long-term (balance sheet) Benefits of stockholder or creditor Multi-step income statement – purpose of categories Types of each cash flow activities (operating vs investing vs financing) Retained earnings formula Good audit opinion Key words associated with useful accounting information Categories of ratio analysis Chapter 2 Topics Key terms – account, element, financial statement line, general ledger, source document Order of accounting cycle Permanent vs temporary accounts Chapter 3 & Appendix C Accrual accounting Revenue recognition principle Expense recognition principle Quality of earnings What is a trial balance Debits & Credits – when debits/credits increase or decrease (multiple choice only) Record transactions – financial statement effects (workout problem) and must know balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow impact Adjusting entries – debit/credits and as well as financial statement effects Closing entries – debit/credits (multiple choice only) Chapter 5 Fraud Fraud triangle Internal controls – purpose, types, examples, responsibility, COSO framework Audit opinion related to internal controls PCAOB What is considered cash Good cash controls Bank reconciliations Chapter 11 (lecture slides 1-21 only) Compare & contrast words from notes Calculate the financial ratios Liquidity – what it means, who is interested in those ratios, and what formulas tell you about a company’s liquidity Solvency - what it means, who is interested in those ratios, and what formulas tell you about a company’s solvency Profitability - who is interested in those ratios Cash conversion cycle – what does this tell us Vertical analysis Horizontal analysis Don’t need to know how to calculate weighted average of shares
